poems.note: The heading on p. 21 describes a request for a reward for earlier poems; these four couplets are separately followed by a new heading. The print's أهناها and أملاها correspond to أهنؤها and أملؤها in the online comparison.
The heading presents an apology for absence; the poem describes a toothache. The print has عناء and شفاء where the online comparison has عنائي and شفائي.
Three couplets are on p. 22 and two continue on p. 23 before a new heading. The print reads للاستعفاء where the online comparison has بلا استعفاء.

The heading calls this a satire on couscous built on a half-line by another writer; it does not identify that writer or specify the borrowed half-line. The seven-couplet work is separately bounded in this printing.
The heading describes a chronogram for the birth of Khayr al-Dīn's son; 1274 AH printed under the verse is an occasion annotation, not independently established as the date of composition.
The heading addresses Aḥmad ibn Abī al-Ḍiyāf about a missed visit and mentions Istanbul. It is not treated here as proof of a composition place.
The heading identifies this as a request to Muḥammad Bayram IV; it is followed by a separately headed seal inscription.
The heading presents these two couplets as a seal inscription for Muṣṭafā Bayram on his appointment. The printed 1271 AH annotation is not independently asserted as a composition date.
